title: Harness detection report
description: Output of `setup_coordinator.py detect-harnesses --json`. Reports presence only; credential validity is never checked.

schema_version.description: Monotonic. Increment on any breaking shape change.

checked_validity.description: Always false. Detection is presence-only by design (no billed inference probe, per vendor_health's D6 constraint). Consumers must not treat state=ready as proof of a valid or unexpired credential.

platform.description: sys.platform of the host that was inspected.

home.description: Home directory that was searched. Recorded because detection is host-local and a report is not portable to another machine.

vendors.description: One entry per <vendor>-local agent found in agents.yaml.

vendor.description: Vendor key derived from the <vendor>-local agents.yaml entry.

cli_command.description: Command searched for on PATH. Reported even when absent so the operator knows what was looked for.

config_artifact.description: Home-relative path checked for this vendor, or null when the vendor declares no detectable configuration location. null is what produces state=unknown.

config_present.description: Null when config_artifact is null — absence of a declared location is not evidence of absence of configuration.

credential_env_var.description: Env var the CLI itself requires, from cli.api_key_env in agents.yaml (e.g. OPENROUTER_API_KEY for pi).

state.description: ready = CLI on PATH and config artifact present. cli_missing = CLI not on PATH. config_missing = CLI present, declared artifact absent. unknown = no declared artifact to check; MUST NOT be conflated with config_missing (design decision D5).

remediation.description: Operator-facing next step, or null. MUST be null when state is unknown — emitting a login instruction for a vendor with no login command is the failure this field exists to avoid.
